video.title: The Most Profitable Business You Can Run From a Phone

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Eli, a former Connecticut real estate agent and truck dispatcher who built a trailer-subleasing business. He leased 53ft semi-trailers from a big lessor for about $350/month, rented them to truckers for about $180/week, and found customers through Facebook Marketplace and then Facebook ads. He claims about 300 trailers, $250k/month in billings and $40-50k/month net profit with two virtual employees, run from his phone. Key takeaways: net-30 supplier terms plus upfront deposits and weekly billing give immediate positive cash flow; GPS tracking and insurance structure matter; paid ads were the scaling lever.

speakers.name: Eli
speakers.description: Runs a trailer rental/subleasing company for truckers; ex real estate agent and truck dispatcher

ideas.name: Semi-trailer subleasing to truckers
ideas.one_liner: Lease 53ft semi-trailers from a large lessor on net-30 terms and sublease them to owner-operator truckers at roughly double the cost, billed weekly with a deposit.
ideas.business_model: Recurring weekly rental (arbitrage between lessor cost and sublease price) plus deposits and early-exit penalties
ideas.customer: Owner-operator truckers and small trucking companies, often new companies or with poor credit, including Spanish-speaking clients
ideas.problem: Truckers need trailers to work; many big rental companies will not rent to new companies or people with weak credit.
ideas.offer: Brand-new or DOT-inspected 53ft dry van, food-grade and flatbed trailers available quickly with flexible credit requirements and weekly billing.

pricing.model: Weekly rental with a deposit and a 3-month minimum term

price_points.label: Cost of leasing a trailer from supplier

pricing.notes: Aim to at least double cost; thirds rule: a third covers the trailer cost, a third expenses/taxes/payroll, a third profit. Prices were held low at first to get customers in, planning to raise later. Deposit forfeited and sometimes a penalty if the client leaves before 3 months.

acquisition_channels.details: Basic Facebook Marketplace posts on his personal page with photos of the trailer inside, outside and tyres, plus year, make, location and 'flexible with new companies'. Boosted posts and multiple posts in different areas. About 10 trailers rented in the first 2 months.

quote.text: I would post a picture of a trailer outside of the trailer and some inside pigs, some some pics of the tires, 53 ft drivein for rent.
quote.speaker: Eli

acquisition_channels.details: Business Facebook page with still-image ad campaigns run nationwide because truckers travel for deals. Spent about $5,000/month at the end for roughly 25 new clients per month.

quote.text: I was spending towards the end 5,000 a month on Facebook ads, which is not a lot. And I was getting probably 25 new clients per month from Facebook ads.
quote.speaker: Eli

acquisition_channels.details: By the end, existing truckers referred other truckers.

ideas.delivery: Trailers are leased from a big supplier (Penske, Ryder, Premier Leasing type companies) and handed to renters at pickup locations across several states (CT, NJ, NY, MA, PA, FL). Trailers are DOT inspected yearly. The supplier handles maintenance on a triple-net basis. One virtual employee ran ads, followed up with leads, sent documents, coordinated billing and pickup; a second virtual employee also worked in the business.
unit_economics_claims: Lease cost about $350/month vs rental about $750/month
Roughly 10 trailers in first 2 months, about $7,500/month recurring
About 100 trailers and $75k/month end of 2020 with $10-15k net
About 300 trailers and $250k/month with $40-50k net profit
$5,000/month ad spend for about 25 new clients, about 10x return on ad spend by interviewer's maths
Startup cost was only the roughly $4,000/year insurance
10-15 of 300 trailers never came back, costing $15-25k each
ideas.startup_cost: About $4,000 for the first year's insurance policy; no deposit needed with the supplier
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Immediate; the first trailer was rented to his uncle in Nov 2019 and about 10 trailers were rented within 2 months

acquisition.how: Facebook Marketplace listings and paid image ads are inbound and can be generated, posted and optimised by agents with occasional human approval; lead follow-up calls were done by a human.

onboarding.how: Contract, insurance certificate and deposit collection can be templated and e-signed; verifying additional-insured status and ID needs some human checks.

delivery.how: Trailers are physical assets that must be picked up, inspected, GPS-tracked, repaired and recovered when missing; software can only coordinate.

billing.how: Weekly recurring card or ACH billing through a payment processor like PaySimple; dunning and reminders can be automated.

support.how: Repair coordination, breakdowns and Spanish-language customer calls need humans, though AI can triage and schedule.

uk_applicability.notes: The model is built on the US trucking market, DOT inspection and US lessors (Penske, Ryder). UK equivalents exist (trailer hire, operator licences, MOT-style annual trailer tests, GB insurance) but supplier terms like net-30 with no deposit may not exist, and the market is smaller. A Bromley-based solo founder cannot realistically run physical trailer logistics remotely.

risks: Theft or loss of trailers (3-5% never returned, $15-25k each)
Insurance gaps: needing additional-insured cover so claims are actually covered
Stripe froze funds; payment processor risk
Customer credit and default risk, deposit disputes
Thin spread requires scale; net margin only about 15-20%

ideas.name: Truck dispatching (load matching)
ideas.one_liner: Match owner-operator truckers with freight from load boards for a roughly 10% margin per load.
ideas.problem: Truckers need loads and do not have time to search load boards.
ideas.offer: Find and negotiate loads for the driver through load boards such as DAT.

pricing.notes: Example load CT to upstate NY paying about $800 with at least a 10% margin. No licence needed for dispatching, only for brokering.

acquisition_channels.details: Not detailed; truckers looking for work contacted him.

ideas.delivery: Done virtually by phone and load boards.
unit_economics_claims: Eli said he was not making much money

acquisition.how: Finding drivers needs outreach; UK PECR limits cold contact to sole traders.

onboarding.how: Driver details and documents can be collected by forms.

delivery.how: Load search can be agent-assisted but rate negotiation by phone is human.

uk_applicability.notes: US load boards and rules; UK has different freight exchanges and operator licensing.

quotes.text: You do need a license to broker loads, which means it's on the other side.
quotes.speaker: Eli

ideas.name: Subleasing other equipment (small trailers, mobile storage, specialised trailers)
ideas.one_liner: Apply the same lease-then-sublease model to motorcycle/utility trailers, mobile storage containers, or hazmat equipment.
ideas.customer: Individuals and businesses needing small trailers or temporary storage
ideas.offer: Rent smaller trailers (15-20 ft) or mobile storage for home projects

uk_applicability.notes: Trailer and container hire exist in the UK with different regulation and competition.

quotes.text: You can do this with storage with storage equipment as well. You can lease mobile storage equipment

tactics.name: Net-30 supplier terms with upfront deposit and weekly billing
steps: Negotiate net-30 payment with the supplier and no deposit
Take a deposit from the customer upfront
Bill the customer weekly from day one so cash flow is positive immediately
Seek triple-net terms where the supplier covers maintenance

quote.text: you want something called triple net, which is that you take care of the maintenance so that your cost on a monthly basis is the lowest possible
quote.speaker: Eli

tactics.name: Facebook Marketplace listing to validate demand
steps: Post simple photos of the asset inside and outside, with year, make and location
Say you are flexible with new companies
Post multiple listings in different areas
Boost the posts
Match inquiries to inventory wherever the driver needs it

tactics.name: Price at 2-3x cost using the thirds rule
steps: Aim to at least double the lease cost, ideally triple
Allocate one third to cost, one third to expenses and taxes, one third to profit
Start with a lower price to get customers into a sticky asset, then raise later

quote.text: You're always trying to double at least double if you can triple because you know you have to think about taxes and insurance fees
quote.speaker: Eli

tactics.name: Minimum term plus deposit to reduce churn
steps: Require a 3-month minimum
Take a $750 deposit forfeited if they leave early
Charge a penalty in some cases

tactics.name: Delegate ads and lead closing to a virtual assistant
steps: Hire bilingual VAs via Upwork, then move them off the platform
One VA runs Facebook ads and calls leads
She sends documents, coordinates billing and pickup

tactics.name: Test the idea before forming the LLC
steps: Get at least one paying customer first
Then form the LLC, bank account and scale the supplier relationship

quote.text: You always have to test your ideas before creating the LLC, creating a bank account and things like that.
quote.speaker: Eli

warnings.warning: Put GPS trackers on every trailer from day one; without them trailers went missing and some were never recovered.

quote.text: in the first year, I didn't even think about putting GPS on the trailers, which is something that I should have done from the first first trailer.
quote.speaker: Eli

warnings.warning: Structure contracts and additional-insured requirements so you are actually covered, not just theoretically covered.

quote.text: so that when something happens, you're actually covered, not theoretically covered.
quote.speaker: Eli

warnings.warning: Stripe froze his funds for no apparent reason, a risk for high-volume businesses.

quote.text: they would freeze my funds over no reason.
quote.speaker: Eli

warnings.warning: Running listings on a personal Facebook page was not scalable or delegatable; use a business page.
He did not tell the supplier he was subleasing at first; it worked out but is a contractual risk.

quote.text: I didn't tell them in the beginning. I just kind of grew the company.
quote.speaker: Eli

lessons.lesson: Ask suppliers what they can do for you (net-30, no deposit, GPS, maintenance); terms that make you cash-flow positive from day one are a huge advantage.

quote.text: Ask them really what can they do for you? What are the terms? Can you do net30?
quote.speaker: Eli

lessons.lesson: Follow customer requests; the business started when his uncle asked for a trailer, and a small test with one client validated demand.
Sticky assets that customers need to earn a living give low churn and tolerance for pricing.
Paid ads were his consistent answer to growth; once unit economics are proven, spend more.

quote.text: The answer for me was putting more money into paid ads. That was always the answer.
quote.speaker: Eli

lessons.lesson: Weekly billing feels smaller to customers and speeds cash collection.
Hire low-cost bilingual virtual staff to cover ads and sales so the owner can work remotely.
Serve underserved segments (new companies, poor credit) that big incumbents decline.
AI agents can now set up much of such a business (contracts, sourcing, ad management), which Eli says would have saved him two years.

quote.text: Any AI really can take you 90% of the way there.
quote.speaker: Eli

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with a coherent story and some specific numbers, but figures are unverified, some revenue claims are rounded or led by the host, and the ROAS maths is the host's estimate. The business was reportedly sold but details are not given.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sponsor read for GoHighLevel; guest says he does not sell a course.
